newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Arab-Malaysian Bank targets tier-I by '98-chairman.
newsitem.headline: Arab-Malaysian Bank targets tier-I by '98-chairman.

text.p: Arab-Malaysian Bank Bhd hopes to achieve tier-I status by 1998 under Malaysia's two-tier banking system, the group's chairman Azman Hashim said.

He told Reuters in an interview on Thursday that the bank, a subsidiary of AMMB Holdings Bhd, was hoping to expand its shareholders' funds to one billion ringgit in two years to qualify for tier-I status.
Its shareholders funds at present exceed 500 million ringgit, the chairman said.
"That (one billion ringgit by 1998) is the first barrier, we want to crash the barrier," he said.
He said various capital raising exercises and a sharp growth in business will help attain that status.
Azman said group member Arab-Malaysian Finance Bhd had already qualified for tier-I status and had applied to Bank Negara, the central bank, for confirmation of its status.
Arab-Malaysian Finance in September announced a bonus issue to capitalise 90.7 million ringgit of its reserves and a rights issue to raise 481.41 million ringgit.
Tier-I banks, merchant banks and finance companies are allowed to operate in a more liberal regulatory environment.
To achieve Tier-I status, banks should have minimum shareholders' funds of 500 million ringgit, which should increase to one billion by the year 2000.
Earlier this month, Bank Negara Malaysia announced new restrictions on finance companies to force them to grow either through mergers or capital mergers.

It said finance companies must raise their shareholders' funds to at least 350 million ringgit ($139 million) by January 1, 1998, to remain eligible for trading in the interbank money market. The requirement would be further increased to 600 million ringgit by January 1, 1999.
This was also in line with the requirement for tier-I status, the central bank said. ($1 = 2.52 ringgit)
